title: 把 LLM eval 擺在 A/B 前面——funnel vs fork、calibration、與那 42% 還是被 rollback 的實驗
summary: Spotify 工程團隊把 LLM eval 重新框成 A/B test 上游的 funnel 而非平行的 fork——eval 抓 tone / intent alignment / trust-breaking、A/B 抓 session / crash / retention，兩層由 calibration 對齊。即使如此仍有 42% 實驗 rollback，因為 eval 看不到 user-level outcome；不做 calibration 的 eval 是 opinion 不是 evidence。
widget_questions: What does the funnel topology look like versus the fork topology in terms of control flow, traffic budget, and decision authority?

Which response-level signals can LLM-as-judge evals see (tone, intent alignment, trust-breaking content), and which user-outcome signals (session length, crash rate, retention, latency p99) stay invisible until A/B test?

As offline-online calibration ρ sweeps from 0 to 1, how does the funnel's experiment hit-rate diverge from a parallel fork's flat baseline, and where does Spotify's 42%-rollback reality sit on this curve?

When eval rubric calibration with real-task outcome is weak, what does the gap between a coding-eval-visible improvement and the true longer-task improvement look like — the Anthropic Opus 4.5 calibration-failure shape?
